config.text: Responsive layout container for horizontal and vertical stacking with gap, alignment, hairline edges, scroll regions (`scrollY` with `maxHeight` is a capped list), cards (`dashed` for an empty one), viewport-tier overrides, and author-writable `visible` and `outline` states for Variants.

Surface container with optional translatable title and description, header, footer, styling variants (`dialog` adds a header description, a close button, header and footer separators and a dimmed backdrop), viewport-tier overrides, and an author-writable `visible` state.
Typography element on the Quiet Canvas scale (display, headline, title, body, ui, label, mono) with tonal accents and translatable text.

Button with translatable label, Lucide icon, optional trailing icon and shortcut hint, neutral-outline default, one solid primary per region (or the solid neutral for a group's current choice), muted or primary link looks, a loading spinner, and 44px targets on touch tiers. Author-writable `disabled`, `visible`, `loading` and `variant` states drive Variants.

Button with translatable label, Lucide icon, optional trailing icon and shortcut hint, neutral-outline default, one solid primary per region (or the solid neutral for a group's current choice), muted or primary link looks, a loading spinner, and 44px targets on touch tiers. Author-writable `disabled`, `visible`, `loading` and `variant` states drive Variants.
Button configuration. `label` accepts an `$i18n` binding (lowered to `labelKey`). `icon` and `trailingIcon` take Lucide names.
labelResult, label, variant, icon, presentation, theme

Status badge, mono identity chip, or count; carries a leading Lucide icon so color is never the only signal. Translated labels may interpolate {value} and the live render context ({viewportId}, {viewport}, {locale}, {theme}).
Text field or textarea with translatable label, placeholder, help and error text, leading Lucide icon, shortcut hint, and an author-writable `invalid` state.
Sidebar navigation row: Lucide icon, translatable label, count badge (annotation-colored for unresolved comments), selection with a 2px Iris inset bar, and an icon-only rail mode.
Hairline separator for dividing layout sections, with viewport-tier overrides.
Round author mark: initials for people, a bot glyph for agents, a cog for the system. Reviewers are never told apart by color alone.
Keyboard shortcut key cap in the mono blueprint register. Keys are literal and never translated; hidden on touch tiers by default.

Comment pin: a 28px Marker teardrop with the starter's initials (or a bot glyph for agents). States: open, ready (notice-blue eye badge), resolved (24px graphite check), pending (dashed). Selected pins get a 2px Iris ring.

Thread bubble: a 320px, 12px-radius overlay card with title, status badge, target chip, timeline body and reply footer. `placement` is anchored (absolute at x/y), sheet (bottom sheet with grip), or inline (detail pane). Author-writable `open` and `status` states drive Variants.

The Workbench canvas: a recessed graphite ground with a 16px dot grid, the previewed View in a 2px-radius lifted frame, an overlay layer for pins and bubbles, a centered floating tool palette, and a bottom-left tray. `mode: "comment"` draws the 2px Marker inset line and shows the hint slot.
Group of Segments rendered as a segmented control, an underline tab strip, or the floating canvas tool palette (pill with overlay shadow).

One option inside a SegmentedControl: Lucide icon, translatable label, count, and shortcut hint. The palette appearance fills Iris when selected, or tints Marker for the Comment tool (`activeTone: "annotation"`).
Phone bottom navigation: a 56px sticky bar of TabBarItems (Overview, Views, UX Flows, Reviews). Shown only on the compact tier unless `showOn: "always"`.
One bottom-navigation destination: a 20px Lucide icon over a 12px label, an optional count badge, and a 2px Iris top bar when selected.

Primary navigation sidebar with header, scrolling content and a Workspace footer group, separated by hairlines. Defaults: 264px on desktop, a 56px icon rail on tablets, hidden on phones (the TabBar takes over).
44px canvas toolbar with a start group (render-context chips) and an end group (session status, zoom, fit). Scrolls horizontally rather than wrapping on narrow tiers.
Render-context chip: icon, muted label and a highlighted value with a select chevron. Translated values may interpolate the live render context ({viewportId}, {viewport}, {locale}, {theme}).
Review thread timeline entry: a message (avatar, author, role badge, relative time, 14px body) or a compact lifecycle event (icon plus one muted line, toned success/info/annotation).

Review thread row: status icon (open/ready/resolved, never color alone), author avatar, one-line title, relative time, annotation-colored message count, meta line, mono anchor and change-domain chips. Selected rows get an Iris tint and inset bar.

Subtle inline alert with a status icon, title, description and an actions slot; `toast: true` renders the floating toast surface, and `dismissible: true` adds a close button that hides the alert and fires `dismiss`. Author-writable `visible` state drives Variants.

Empty state with a muted icon disc, title, description and one next action. `dashed: true` draws the 1px dashed "nothing authored yet" boundary; `compact: true` is the one-line dashed block for an empty list inside a page (no icon disc, a quiet title). Author-writable `visible` state drives Variants.
A Lucide icon by name from the Kit icon set, with a size and a tone. It is decorative unless it has a `label`, which becomes its accessible name (`role="img"`).

Loading placeholder block with a width, a height and a corner radius. With a `label` it is a named `status` region (`aria-busy`); without one it is hidden from assistive technology. The pulse stops under reduced motion.

One generic row for lists, timelines, step lists and trees: `leading`, `content` and `trailing` slots, an indent `level`, a `divided` hairline, a row height (`size`), top alignment of the end slots (`align`), a neutral current-row look (`selectedLook`), and author-writable `selected`, `dimmed` and `visible` states. `interactive` makes the row one focusable, pressable target that fires `click`.

Native checkbox with a translatable label and description, a literal mono `meta` at the end, a `warning` description tone, a mono label (`mono`), a 44px row target (`touch`), and author-writable `checked`, `indeterminate` and `disabled` states. A press writes `checked` and fires `toggle`.

Select trigger with a translatable label, help and placeholder, the chosen value as literal text (a multiple select joins its values with a comma and a space), required, invalid and disabled flags, and an author-writable `open` state that shows its SelectOption children as a listbox panel. The trigger fires `toggle`.

One option of a Select listbox: a translatable label (optionally mono, as an Event name is) with a translatable description line under it, a check while `selected`, and a `disabled` flag. A press fires `click`; the author-writable `selected` state drives Variants.

Disclosure: a header button with a chevron (before the label, or after it with `chevron: "end"`), an optional leading icon, a translatable label that may interpolate `{value}`, and a literal trailing `meta` (a count or a status), above a `content` slot. `appearance: "link"` is the link-style toggle. The author-writable `open` state shows the content; the header press writes it and fires `toggle`.

Literal text in the mono face (JSON, a diff, a log), shown exactly as authored and never translated. A long line scrolls sideways or wraps; `maxHeight` bounds the block, which then scrolls and is focusable. With a `label` it is a named region.

Column grid for TableRow widgets: `columns` is the CSS grid template every row follows, so cells line up, and `minWidth` is the width below which the table scrolls sideways. Cells are other Widgets, so it is exposed as a named list of rows.

One row of a Table: its `cells` slot holds the cell Widgets, laid out on the table's column grid. `header` styles it as the column headings; `align: "start"` top-aligns the cells of a tall row; the author-writable `selected` and `visible` states mark the current row and show or hide it.

One change of a semantic diff: an operation (added, removed, changed or moved) with its icon, tone and translated words, the translated field name, the changed thing as literal mono text, a struck `before` and inserted `after` value, and a list of finer `changes`. Values are content and are never translated.
A path of steps in a named navigation landmark, one BreadcrumbItem per step. A long path scrolls sideways, so the landmark itself is the focusable scroller.

One step of a Breadcrumb: its number, a variant (the state the step shows), a label (what it belongs to), a trailing note and an optional Lucide icon. The author-writable `current` state marks the step the path ends on (`aria-current="step"`).

A static projection of a node-and-edge graph on the canvas ground, drawn like the Workbench's UX Flow graph: nodes on an explicit column and row grid with an entry flag, a variant chip, a problem count and an end or unreachable mark, and routed edges with mono trigger labels. A node or an edge label writes the `selection` state and fires `select`; arrow keys travel along edges.

A picture from an image Asset: `source` is an Asset-bound field, so the author binds an Asset and the Workspace resolves it. Translatable alternative text (empty for a decorative image), a size, a fit and a radius. Without a resolved source it shows a dashed placeholder.

accessibility: Every Catalog row is one pressable target that states whether its detail is open by its chevron and its position; the detail tables are named lists of rows.
A usage count is text in a badge, so it is never conveyed by color alone; the raw JSON Schema is a named, focusable region.
constraints: Built only from Adapter Widgets (Stack, Text, Icon, Badge, ListItem, Table, TableRow, TextInput, Disclosure, CodeBlock, EmptyState, Skeleton); no Widget outside the Adapter catalog.
Every visible string is bound with $i18n except identities (Widget types, Adapter IDs, schema fields, View names); en-US and zh-TW keep identical key sets.
This View models the page content only; the Workbench shell is shown by the Workbench View. The detail is modelled for one entry (Button).
Visual language follows the Quiet Canvas design system in DESIGN.md.
entryConditions: A person opened the Catalog destination (the Catalog entry of the command palette), a deep link of the Components section (/workspace/product-kit?section=components#product-kit-catalog); the page scrolls to the Catalog block, so this View shows the block without the page title and section tabs above it.

The base state is the dogfood Workspace as it is: the 39 Catalog entries of its one valid Adapter, each collapsed, for a member who may read the Workspace. The usage counts are those of the dogfood Views before this change.
The render context selects one Workspace viewport preset, one Locale and one theme; the Workbench renders the live page and this View is its design reference.
spec.intent: Show the Component Catalog block of the Workbench Product Kit page as built from Adapter Widgets only: one row per Widget type of the active Adapters, each opening its detail in place, with a filter, and the states where the Catalog is loading, unavailable or has no match.
interactionRules: Each Catalog row opens its detail in place: Adapter, type, description, Config schema, properties, state, Events, i18n mapping, Asset fields, the Views that use it and its Catalog problems.
A filter narrows the rows by type, Adapter or description and says when nothing matches.
While the Adapter set is invalid or unchecked the Catalog is unavailable and shows no partial list; the Catalog is read-only and nothing here edits an entry.
